concerns.text: T002 lists `textstat` and `evalue` in requirements. The plan.md explicitly rejects `textstat` in favor of the `polite` library for robustness checks (Section 'Complexity Tracking'). Including `textstat` introduces an unauthorized dependency that contradicts the approved technical approach, violating the plan's constraint on fallback classifiers.

T019c implements conditional z-scoring (global vs. per-source) based on a Kolmogorov-Smirnov test. FR-002 mandates a single standardized `mean_politeness_score` per conversation without conditional logic. This task introduces a branching logic that may result in per-source scores, violating the deterministic output requirement of FR-002.

T032a specifies `textstat` as the fallback for LIWC-2015. While plan.md authorizes `polite` as a substitute, T032a selects `textstat` (a different library) without explicit authorization in the plan or spec. This constitutes a silent scope drift and violates the constraint on linguistic feature extraction consistency (Constitution Principle VII).

T027a states that if the fallback model (fixed-effects) is used, it 'does NOT count toward the SC-003 ≥95% convergence rate metric'. SC-003 requires the system to report a convergence rate based on 'per sensitivity analysis run'. Excluding a run from the metric calculation makes the criterion unmeasurable as defined in the spec, violating the success criterion's intent.

T001 is marked `[X]` (complete) in the artifact, yet the 'REJECTED' section of the input report states no evidence exists for the creation of the listed directories. A task marked complete without evidence of execution violates the Data Hygiene principle (Constitution Principle III) and the requirement for verifiable state.
